idea-plugin.name: Dev Runner for Apache Tomcat
idea-plugin.description:
Runs a Maven WAR module on a local Apache Tomcat 10/11 straight from your build output, with hot reload of Java and Angular changes.

No packaging, no copying, no project changes. The plugin generates a private Tomcat base for development and mounts your sources directly into the webapp:
  • target/classes of the WAR module and of every jar module it depends on
  • Maven runtime libraries (provided/test scopes and container jars are excluded)
  • src/main/webapp and the Angular build output (read from angular.json)
  • Maven-filtered context.xml / WEB-INF files from target/<finalName>
Hot reload
  • Save a Java file → only its module is compiled → HotSwap when debugging.
  • Structural changes (new fields, methods, endpoints, beans) → automatic context reload through JMX in a few seconds, without restarting Tomcat. Works in Run mode too.
  • Angular: start ng build --watch from the IDE; browser caching is disabled for development.
Configuration
  • Run configuration Tomcat Dev with Run and Debug, plus an automatic Build before launch.
  • Tomcat, server.xml and context.xml are auto-detected in their usual locations (CATALINA_HOME, tomcat-maven-plugin, maven-war-plugin, META-INF) and can be overridden.
  • Existing JNDI resources and parameters in context.xml are preserved.
Local configuration outside the project
  • Per-webapp folder ~/.tomcat-dev/<project>/<app>: env.properties, context.xml, webapp/, classes/, lib/ override the project's files without modifying them, so local database URLs, ports or credentials are never committed.
  • ${...} templates (context.xml, web.xml, …) are filtered by the plugin with the Maven filter files and the local env.properties: no Maven build needed.
  • Several WAR modules on one Tomcat; only the webapps containing changed modules are reloaded.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
2.3.1
  • Fix: resources that the WAR build copies into WEB-INF/classes with maven-war-plugin webResources (application.properties, logback.xml, …) and that are not in target/classes are now on the classpath.
  • Fix: resource sets in context.xml, server.xml or the global conf/context.xml that point to a missing file (e.g. an old jar version in ~/.m2) are ignored with a warning instead of stopping Tomcat.
  • Fix: a META-INF/context.xml copied into the WAR by maven-war-plugin webResources is now used instead of the one in src/main/webapp (its Parameter and Environment entries were missing).
  • Fix: a conf/web.xml in Tomcat home that already contains the no-cache filter no longer stops the webapps.
  • Fix: server.xml and context.xml split into several files with XML entity includes are fully used (included parts were dropped). conf/<Engine>/<Host>/context.xml.default is copied too.
  • No deprecated API usages anymore (ReadAction.run, XDebugSession.getRunContentDescriptor).
  • Fix: structural class changes (new field, record component, method, lambda…) are detected from the compiled classes and reload the context. IntelliJ could report such a HotSwap as successful, leaving old and new classes mixed (NoSuchMethodError).
  • With the Angular watch on, a warning is logged when the Before-launch Maven goal would rebuild the front end or clean; the form shows the recommended goal (package -DskipTests -Dskip.npm -Dskip.installnodenpm).
2.3.0
  • Local configuration folder outside the project per webapp (env.properties, context.xml, webapp/, classes/, lib/) and a project-level server.xml; Create Local Config action creates env.properties.
  • The plugin filters ${...} templates itself (Maven filter files + local env.properties); no Maven build needed.
  • Several WAR modules on one Tomcat; context reload limited to the webapps containing changed modules.
  • Clearer run configuration form: defaults shown inside empty fields, examples on separate lines, home folder paths shown as ~/ in the form and the log.
2.2.0
  • Renamed to Dev Runner for Apache Tomcat; English user interface and documentation.
  • Plugin icon, Marketplace metadata, signing and publishing configuration.
2.1.1
  • Disable browser caching of static files in the development Tomcat (no project changes).
2.1.0
  • Context reload through JMX for structural Java changes; four reload modes.
2.0.0
  • Standalone Tomcat run configuration (no SmartTomcat needed); sources mounted instead of copied.
